value: The immediate environment and shadow of the supermassive black hole at the center of galaxy M87.
Can the shadow of a supermassive black hole be directly imaged, and does its size match the prediction of general relativity?

Presents the first direct image of a black hole shadow, obtained with Earth-sized very-long-baseline interferometry, confirming a bright emission ring of the size predicted by general relativity for the supermassive black hole in M87.

quote: We observed M87* on 2017 April 5, 6, 10, and 11 with the EHT.
Our radiowave observations thus provide powerful evidence for the presence of supermassive black holes in centers of galaxies and as the central engines of active galactic nuclei.
When surrounded by a transparent emission region, black holes are expected to reveal a dark shadow caused by gravitational light bending and photon capture at the event horizon.

value: the first images are made by four teams working independently and without interaction, in the authors' words to minimize shared bias - and each team nonetheless recovered a ring of similar diameter brightened to the south
quote: In the first stage, four teams worked independently to reconstruct * the first EHT images of M87 using an early engineering data release. The teams worked without interaction to minimize shared bias, yet each produced an image with a similar feature: a ring of diameter ∼38–44 μas with prominent enhanced brightness to the south

value: a parameter combination is admitted to the Top-Set only if it both fits the observed data AND reconstructs four known geometries - ring, crescent, filled disk, asymmetric double - from synthetic data, so the imaging parameters are validated against ground truth and not only against the object under study
quote: We determined a “Top- Set” of parameter combinations that both produced images of M87* that were consistent with the observed data and that reconstructed accurate images from synthetic data sets corresponding to four known geometric models (ring, crescent, filled disk, and asymmetric double source).

value: because the reconstructed resolutions differ between pipelines, each image is blurred with a circular Gaussian to one common and deliberately conservative resolution before use
quote: Because the angular resolutions of the reconstructed images vary among the pipelines, we blurred each image with a circular Gaussian to a common, conservative angular resolution of 20 μas.

value: systematic baseline error is measured rather than assumed: three independent fringe-fitting pipelines, two polarizations and two frequency bands are compared against each other, and the residual disagreement between them IS the quoted systematic
quote: Comparisons between the three independent pipelines, the two polarizations, and the two frequency bands enabled estimation of systematic baseline errors of around 1° in visibility phase and 2% for visibility amplitudes.

value: the two frequency bands are correlated on two separate software correlators at two institutions, and a few identical scans are passed through both so that any difference between the correlators would show up as a disagreement on the same input
quote: Correlation of the data was carried out using a software correlator (Deller et al. 2007) at the MIT Haystack Observatory and at für Radioastronomie, each handling one of the two frequency bands. Differences between the two independent correlators were shown to be negligible through the exchange of a few identical scans for cross comparison.

value: one highly sensitive station is used as the array's reference station, which is what enabled the ionospheric and tropospheric corrections at the other sites
quote: Using ALMA as a highly sensitive reference station enabled critical corrections for ionospheric and tropospheric distortions at the other sites.

quote: For these models we produced simulated visibilities for the April 11 schedule and weather parameters and calibrated them with a synthetic data generation and calibration pipeline (Blecher et al. 2017; Janssen et al. 2019; Roelofs et al. 2019a). The simulated data were then imaged with the same pipeline used for the observed images.
